groups.joined:
Riders who use more than one transit agency in a single trip (e.g., BART to Muni) will only be charged full fare on the first operator. A transfer discount of up to $2.85 will apply on any additional transit agency the rider uses within a two-hour window. This discount is available when using Tap and Ride (contactless bank cards, Apple Pay and Google Pay) and Clipper card users once their cards has been upgraded to the new system, a process customers can initiate by logging into your account on the new account-based
Clipper website
.

Low income adults earning 200% or less of the federal poverty level get 50% off through the regional
Clipper START program
.

Youth 5-18 years old get 50% off with a
Youth Clipper card
. 4 years and younger ride free. (Search for the various locations where you can apply and immediately receive a discount card by selecting "Staffed Locations" under "Location Type" for Youth and Senior card services. They are also available by mail)

Seniors 65 and over get 62.5% off with a
Senior Clipper card
. (Search for the various locations where you can apply and immediately receive a discount card by selecting "Staffed Locations" under "Location Type" for Youth and Senior card services. They are also available by mail)

The
Clipper Access card
(formerly known as RTC) is a version of Clipper created for passengers under 65 with qualifying disabilities to provide 62.5% off.

BART offers a “High-value Discount.” Adult Clipper cards get a 6.25% discount on cash value rides by buying $48 worth of value for $45 or $64 worth of value for $60 when autoload is set up with your registered Clipper card. You can only purchase an HVD ticket
online by setting up Autoload
or through a transit benefit program. In your Clipper account, select "Add Value" and select “Transit Pass” then “BART” and then the amount of HVD you want.

Students on a
school-sponsored field trip
for an educational purpose are eligible for a 62.5% discount fare when purchased in advance through Group Sales.

BART is part of
Clipper BayPass
, the region’s first prepaid, all-system transit pass, to employers, colleges, and affordable housing developments.

-
Sign up for Clipper
-
Access Clipper Account
-
Clipper Customer Service

Youth and Senior Clipper cards can be obtained
by mail
or there are
multiple locations across the Bay Area
where you can apply and immediately receive a Youth or Senior card. Applicants will need to bring documentation verifying age eligibility (for example: driver’s license, photo ID card or birth certificate).

In August 2025, BART became the Bay Area's first
Tap and Ride
system, meaning riders now have the ability to pay adult fares at BART fare gates using physical contactless credit or debit cards or mobile payment methods, such as Apple Pay and Google Pay.
Those with eligibility-based discounts must continue using their physical or digital Clipper card.
Allowing discount card holders to join Tap and Ride is on the roadmap, but it is not yet available.
